Orlghelovar (I12)

Region (English scoring-table region): Serpentspine.

In a sentence: Rekindle the lost cobalt Dwarven glass-city, then turn an ancient craft into a research state spanning trade, medicine, and artifice.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Long (89 direct I12 mission definitions, including phase conditions) | Mission-tree update: use the local scripts for EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Degree of confinement: Medium-high (Hold restoration, research, and building requirements) | Early pressure: Depends on the Adventurer predecessor | Expansion capacity: Above average, focused on industry and trade networks

The Ancient Hold and the Country Today

The “Glasslords” of the offline English Wiki first refer to an ancient Serpentspine Hold: cobalt Dwarves made blue glass, traded across Bulwar, and studied natural sciences at the University of Guntîrhug. Lenses and reflectors even brought sunlight underground. That wealth later became a weakness when the Hold neglected its defenses; it fell in 2686 Before the Calendar. This is the history of the ancient Hold, not evidence that I12 already existed as a full country in 1444. [Wiki account]

The current base Mod treats I12 as a country that can be formed after a qualified Dwarven Adventurer company reclaims the old Hold. The formation decision requires control of the relevant Hold, sufficient administrative technology, and Adventurer conditions. On formation, the country becomes Cobalt Dwarven and receives a replacement mission tree. I12's country-history template specifies a republic, an Adventurer reform, Ancestor Worship, and the old Hold as its capital; that template defines the formable's attributes, but does not by itself prove that it can be selected directly at the 1444 start. Which Adventurer company arrives first depends on the campaign. [Local scripts]

From Glassworks to a Research System

The opening is not simply “mine gems and get rich.” “Restart the Glassworks” restores glass as the capital's trade good; workshops, veins, and production buildings become the foundation for later missions. The tree gradually expands cobalt and glass supply, reconnecting the old craft with surface markets. Trade opportunities with Bulwari merchants, Dwarven ports, and forest-dwelling peoples also keep this mountain city from remaining isolated. [Local scripts] [Local flavour text]

The mid-campaign shift is to treat glass as a platform for science. The university, doctors, and researchers become central to the country. “Mana Glass” introduces magical materials and a substantial financial threshold, while glass rifles bring laboratory results to the battlefield. Later research turns to azhalngiv—the material Cannorians call damestear—and Black Damestear, alongside anti-magic materials. This is neither a pure mage state nor merely a Dwarven Hold with ordinary artillery: production, medicine, material science, and artifice are woven into one development path. [Local scripts]

Costs of the Campaign and the Country's Boundaries

The campaign requires both industrial accumulation and expansion beyond the old Hold: obtain glass, diamonds, and scarce materials, and establish trade or territorial connections with nearby Holds and Bulwar. War is a means of opening access to resources and routes; what continually demands the player's attention is construction, trade goods, research investment, and phased requirements. Older player posts often advise preparing surface glass provinces and relations with Ovdal Tûngr in advance, but those reports span different Mod versions and include save games altered with console commands. They are not hard requirements for the current missions. [Local scripts] [Community opinion]

The ancient Hold's fall belongs to Wiki history; lasers, glass weapons, and a trade empire rebuilt by the player belong to the mission-tree future. The Halann map also lists relevant source materials, but its reconstructions of intermediate borders and the sequence of disasters have not been checked claim by claim against the original documents and should not be presented as inevitable outcomes.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 75/100 | Autocracy 50/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 12/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 94/100) | Pluralism 68/100.

The v2.1 values assessment is Good (73/100), with a stable trajectory. The university, medicine, and the living conditions created by trade provide public benefits; open commerce and text welcoming non-Dwarven settlers support relatively broad recognition. Armament and competition for resources reduce restraint, but wealth or technology does not automatically earn a good-alignment score. Education, medicine, and comparatively open inter-species commerce serve the public good. The pursuit of resources abroad and the arms race still limit restraint. Research itself does not automatically make a country good, and artifice intensity is a separate question from ethical assessment.

This country suits players who enjoy Dwarven restoration, industrial chains, trade, science, and a late-campaign turn toward artifice and weapons. If you dislike the Hold's preparatory construction, resource thresholds, or long waits, or only want a short Dwarven conquest campaign, this tree will feel drawn out.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundaries

Official Dev Diary #37 directly introduces its glass trade and research direction; Dev Diary #94 adds background on the ancient Cobalt Dwarven exodus. Two player discussions from 2023–2024 mainly support the impression that the industrial-artifice path is enjoyable but requires advance resource preparation. They are not an audit of today's numbers. [Official development diaries] [Community opinion]

Detailed scripts, fixed-revision Wiki evidence, and player posts are listed on the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Orlghelovar (I12) — Cobalt Ideas

Set ID: I12_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = I12

Cobalt Traditions

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

  • Institution embracement cost: -20% (embracement_cost; raw value -0.2).

1. The Lords of Glass

In the past, the dwarves of Orlghelovar were known as the "Glasslords". It is said they mastered the art of glassmaking and taught its secrets to humans who helped it eventually flourish in places like the Bulwar. As their name implies, the Cobalt dwarves were fond of using cobalt as a pigment, most famously in dark blue Orlghelovar glass - it is said that many ancient human glass relics can trace their origins to the renowned hold.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

2. Seekers of Knowledge

The Cobalt Dwarves were innovative pioneers within the Dwarovar. While some dwarves drew complacent with the power and reach of the empire, within Orlghelovar research of the unknown natural world was still ongoing. Many papers outlining discoveries in physics and other arcane subjects constantly drafted, outlining topics such as Halanna's breath or the applications of mystical plants harvested in the Deepwoods by their Flint neighbours.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Lessons of Decadence

It is said that Orlghelovar was one of the richest holds in the Dwarovar, and was so concerned with their greed and arrogance with trade with the rising kingdoms of Bulwar, it fell with ease to the orc and goblin hordes lack of due diligence repairs on their gates and providing meagre supplies to their army. Their greed and decadence serves as a warning to all dwarves up to this day.

  • Reform progress growth: +15% (reform_progress_growth; raw value 0.15).

4. Glasshammer Fair

In order to keep ties to lucrative markets the lords of Orlghelovar fostered relations with their key market: the richest and most decadent holds of Aul-Dwarov. In 6735 BA the master glassmaker and head of the Glasshammer cartel, Okkid Glasshammer, set up a yearly convention in Amldihr showcasing the new goods and styles from the hold in Orlghelovar. This eventually became the foremost gathering of glassmakers and glass-buyers across the empire, with many a masterpiece ordered during the event.

For Orlghelovar, however, it also kept them in the loop with the coming-and-goings of the rest of the Dwarovar.

  • Global institution spread: +10% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.1).

  • Foreign trade power: +10% (global_foreign_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

5. Reflecting Daylight

Daylight is a pleasure not many dwarves can experience except for some select surface holds, as it is found only beyond the hold's gates. Not so in Orlghelovar where the Cobalt Dwarves developed contraptions using mirrors and lenses to fill their hold with daylight and replace artificial light sources, providing a bright and unique environment. The daylight brought new life to the hold, with indoor flora growing where it couldn't before which became an experience that many dwarves desired for their own homes.

  • State maintenance: -25% (state_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.25).

6. Blowers of Glass and Trumpets

Glassblowing requires strong lungs, which can be used for other purposes as well. It is no surprise then that the Cobalt dwarves were famed wind instrumentalists, the sound of their trumpets and horns echoing deep underground. When they marched to war, they were led by dedicated marching bands which greatly inspired the troops and improved their organisation.

  • morale_damage_received：-10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

7. Guntîrhug

Guntîrhug, the renowned university of Orlghelovar, attracted many dwarves from all over the Dwarovar, as many of the greatest experts of their fields gathered and lectured there. While in other holds they specialised at staring into the sky or in inventing engineering contraptions, all fields of science for researching and documenting the natural world were holistically represented within Guntîrhug. Many students were infamously said to have superiority complexes from staying among the greatest intellectuals, known to repel many peers beyond Guntîrhug. Regardless, such a holistic and wide-ranging education did have many benefits to both students and to Orlghelovar.

  • Technology cost: -5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.05).
